summary: FireHarmony is an open-source wildfire intelligence platform that reconciles 25 years (2001-2026) of incompatible NASA MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active-fire detections into one consistent Burning-Activity Calendar. Because VIIRS resolves 3-5x more small fires (<15 MW) than MODIS, stacking raw satellite counts creates a false 4x wildfire surge in 2012 (38,120 MAE), distorting climate baselines and misdirecting firefighting resources. Validated across 32.64 million NASA FIRMS records in Vietnam, the Amazon, and Australia (and extensible worldwide via custom coordinates), FireHarmony repairs legacy Day-31 API gaps, treats missing satellite passes as Unknown rather than zero fire, and applies a causal Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (STAN) that cuts calibration error by 89.1% down to 4,155 MAE. It empowers firefighters, forest rangers, and researchers with seasonal anomaly heatmaps, polygon filtering, a 6-tool Sensor Lab, and a zero-hallucination AI investigator.

Open-Source Repository (MIT): https://github.com/KienPC1234/FireHarmony

1. What It Does & How It Works

Wildfire agencies and climate scientists rely on two generations of NASA orbital thermal sensors to track global burning over the past quarter-century:

  • NASA MODIS (Terra & Aqua, 2000-present): Scans at 1 km nadir resolution (stretching up to 5 km off-nadir), reliably capturing large fire fronts but missing small understory and agricultural burns.
  • NASA/NOAA VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, 2012-present): Scans at a sharp 375 m resolution across the entire swath, detecting 3x to 5x more low-intensity fires (<15 MW FRP) than MODIS over the exact same landscape.

When raw MODIS and VIIRS records are combined on a single timeline, 2012 appears as a fake 4x global wildfire explosion (38,120 Mean Absolute Error). FireHarmony eliminates this optical illusion and constructs a unified 25-Year Burning-Activity Calendar (2001-2026) through a three-stage scientific pipeline:

  1. Audited Multi-Decadal Archive (32.64M NASA Rows): We ingested and checksum-verified 32,639,009 NASA FIRMS detections across 7,484 CSV files spanning three benchmark regions (Vietnam: 3.57M rows; Amazon: 8.43M rows; Australia: 20.63M rows, each backfilled to 180/180 full paired months from 2012 to 2026) while supporting any region worldwide via live custom coordinates or CSV upload.
    • Tier 1 (b2_seasonal_ratio / STAT): Fast, transparent monthly ratio scaling that cuts raw MODIS error by 88.0% (from 38,120 to 4,581 MAE) and powers instant on-the-fly calibration for custom global polygons.
    • Tier 2 (hts_anchor_v1 / HTS): Hierarchical Tile Scaling across 1,125 local spatial tiles that captures fine regional land-cover differences while preserving area-wide totals (4,525 MAE).
    • Tier 3 (stan_safe_v1 / STAN): Our lightweight 171,362-parameter Spatio-Temporal Attention Network. Using a 12-month MODIS input window, FiLM calendar-month conditioning, and a 3-layer causal Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN, dilations 1, 2, 4) with past-only attention, STAN predicts a bounded residual adjustment over the HTS anchor with Negative Binomial (NB2) uncertainty bounds. Across 72 blind holdout months (2024-2025), STAN reduces error to 4,155 MAE (-89.1% vs. raw MODIS, -9.3% vs. seasonal baseline).

2. Benefits & Intended Real-World Impact

  • For Firefighters & Forest Rangers: Instead of reacting after a wildfire grows out of control, rangers use the Year x Month Burning Calendar to compare the current month against the 20-year historical baseline for that exact same calendar month (e.g., April 2024 vs. historical Aprils). Automatic anomaly flags (|Z| >= 2) reveal early dry-season escalations so crews can pre-position equipment, clear firebreaks, and prioritize high-risk districts.
  • For Local Communities & Disaster Planners: Eliminating the artificial 2012 sensor jump prevents misallocated emergency budgets and provides clear, bilingual (English / Vietnamese) risk summaries and one-click PDF, Markdown, and CSV briefings.
  • For Climate & Earth-Observation Researchers: Provides a reproducible, audit-logged 25-year fire activity series with explicit uncertainty bounds and SHA-256 data provenance.

3. How Our Project Is Creative

  • Anchor-Plus-Residual Safety (AI That Cannot Run Wild): Pure deep-learning models often hallucinate extreme counts during unprecedented El Nino droughts. By locking AI predictions to a bounded residual correction atop a physical-statistical spatial anchor (HTS), FireHarmony combines physical stability with seasonal adaptability.
  • 6-Tool Interactive Sensor Lab: Goes beyond a static dashboard by giving users an interactive laboratory: Sensor X-Ray (MODIS vs. VIIRS split), Blind Sensor Replay (2024-2025 holdout verification), Mission Simulator (stress-testing how calibration holds up if the aging Terra satellite retires or cloud cover hits 50%), Coverage Blind Spots, Spatial Check, and Custom CSV Upload.
  • Zero-Hallucination AI Scientific Investigator: Unlike generic chatbots that guess statistics, our deterministic Python Grounding Engine computes all hotspot totals, k-ratios, and Z-scores first. The LLM only narrates verified telemetry and is strictly constrained to remind users that thermal hotspots measure burning activity, not total burned area (hectares).

4. Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Discovery & Repair of the "Day-31 Bug": While auditing historical pulls, we discovered that standard 5-day NASA FIRMS API loops (days 1-5, 6-10, ..., 26-30) silently skipped Day 31 across seven months of every year (~3.2% missing historical days). We built an automated calendar-aware repair pipeline (fetch_missing.py) and an immutable daily request ledger (request_ledger.jsonl) to close every gap.
  • Honest Missing-Data Guardrails (Null != 0): Cloud cover and orbital outages look identical to zero fire if left unmarked. FireHarmony records unobserved days as Unknown (null), excludes months below 90% paired coverage from climate baselines, and displays "Insufficient Evidence" in the telemetry inspector whenever paired satellite passes are missing.
  • Universal Accessibility: Designed with colorblind-safe Cividis and Viridis scientific palettes, keyboard navigation, responsive mobile layouts, and full EN/VI localization.

5. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Backend & Scientific Computing: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, PyTorch (STAN model & NB2 loss), NumPy, Pandas, Apache Arrow / PyArrow (Parquet columnar caching for sub-second queries over 32.64M rows).
  • Frontend & Geospatial Visualization: TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Leaflet & React-Leaflet (Esri World Imagery, Dark Canvas, and World Topo Terrain layers + custom polygon drawing), Tailwind CSS, KaTeX, Lucide Icons.
  • Infrastructure, Security & QA Testing: Linux workstation (Intel Xeon / NVIDIA GPU for STAN training, CPU inference in production), PM2 process manager, Tailscale Funnel HTTPS, Cloudflare Turnstile bot protection on live compute endpoints, 146 backend pytest tests, 18 Vitest unit tests, and 44 Playwright end-to-end browser tests.

6. Verification & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

  • Open-Source Reproducibility: Released under the MIT License with a SHA-256 verified dataset manifest (download_and_verify.py) so judges and researchers can reproduce every table and chart offline.
  • SI Usage Disclosure: Super Intelligence tools (Google Gemini / Antigravity) were used to assist with code refactoring, automated test authoring, bilingual documentation polishing, and conceptual graphic assets (explicitly labeled on slides). All data auditing, mathematical formulation, model training, and verification were designed and validated by Team Alpha Centauri AB.
